title: U2 - A build step, recorded and reversible
outcome: The front end builds from typed source with a pinned three-package toolchain. The built page is committed, and continuous integration proves it is byte-identical to a clean rebuild, so a hand-edited bundle cannot enter the tree. The new application is reachable behind a server flag at a non-default route. The contract test from MS-0008 passes against both pages.
notInScope: The default page does not change: the root route still serves the page that ships today, and that file is left byte-untouched so the existing implementation-pinning assertions stay green. No container change and no new runtime dependency in the image. No static-asset route in the server - the served page remains the single file the server already reads, and the closed route allow-list is preserved. No feature work in the new application beyond what the contract test requires.
completionEvidence: A clean checkout runs install, build and a difference check against the committed page with no difference. The existing script-parse test still passes against the built page: exactly one bare script element, and the script parses under a syntax check. The dependency audit is clean at high severity. The decision record, the technical plan and the five reversibility conditions are merged. Reverting the build commit leaves a working product, demonstrated rather than asserted.

metadata.risk: Two existing tests discriminate between bundlers and their output. The suite matches a bare script element, so a module-typed script matches nothing; and it runs a syntax check on the extracted script as an ordinary script file, where a top-level import is a syntax error. The bundle must therefore be emitted in the immediately-invoked format. Verify against real build output as the first commit of this milestone, before a single component is written - not after, and never quietly at the flip.
metadata.whySingleFile: Emitting one self-contained committed file avoids adding the product's first static-asset handler, which would be a new route on the trust boundary and the usual place traversal defects appear. It also avoids a container build stage, which would reintroduce the platform-specific package problem the image already works around.
